original_question: The moduli space M^BGGG_{P_1} of irreducible SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons on the BGGG manifold is non-compact. Can this moduli space be compactified, and what bubbling behavior occurs as one or both of the parameters f_1^+ and g_1^+ tend to infinity? In particular, does one obtain bubbling phenomena analogous to those proved for the Bryant-Salamon case, possibly related to anti-self-dual instantons on Taub-NUT?
target_in_paper: Section 4.4, open problem (f): compactify the noncompact BGGG moduli-space end by studying the family from Theorem 7 as one or both of the local parameters f1^+ and g1^+ tend to infinity, with expected Bryant–Salamon-type bubbling and a possible relation to ASD instantons on Taub–NUT. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the BGGG moduli problem, the non-compactness issue, the role of the parameters f1^+ and g1^+, and the paper’s expected analogy with the Bryant–Salamon bubbling phenomenon, including the possible Taub–NUT connection. Those are exactly the ingredients named in Section 4.4(f), with Theorem 7 supplying the relevant nonempty unbounded family and Theorem 6 supplying the comparison bubbling picture. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
missing_details: The gauge group should be stated explicitly: Theorem 7 concerns G2-instantons with gauge group SU(2), not arbitrary gauge group. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The instantons should be identified as irreducible, SU(2)^2 × U(1)-invariant, globally defined on the BGGG metric on R^4 × S^3, with bounded curvature, and smoothly extending over the singular orbit on P1. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

P1 should be defined if the question is to be stand-alone: it is the homogeneous bundle P_lambda = SU(2)^2 ×_(Delta SU(2), lambda) SU(2) with lambda equal to the trivial homomorphism 1. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The parameters f1^+ and g1^+ are local expansion coefficients near the singular orbit: in Lemma 3 one has f^+(t) = f1^+ t + O(t^3) and g^+(t) = g1^+ t + O(t^3) for connections extending over P1. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

To stay closest to the paper, the compactification question should be tied to the family from Theorem 7, i.e. the known unbounded family of global bounded-curvature solutions, rather than to an already fully described moduli space. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

Section 4.4(d) says the full moduli space M_P1^{BGGG} is not yet completely described, because the region 0 < f1^+ - 1/2 < g1^+ < f1^+ is still open; so the sharp paper-faithful formulation is about compactifying the known noncompact end, or the full moduli space once that gap is resolved. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

If one wants to mirror the Bryant–Salamon comparison exactly, one should specify the expected bubbling locus and rescaling picture: bubbling transverse to the associative S^3 = {0} × S^3, as in Theorem 6. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

A fully sharpened version may also mention the away-from-the-bubble limit, since Theorem 6 includes convergence on compact subsets of (R^4 \ {0}) × S^3 to a limiting G2-instanton, not only the local bubble. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
refined_question: On the BGGG G2-manifold R^4 × S^3, let P1 denote the homogeneous SU(2)-bundle over the singular orbit S^3 = {0} × S^3 corresponding to the trivial homomorphism in P_lambda = SU(2)^2 ×_(Delta SU(2), lambda) SU(2). Consider the nonempty unbounded family from Theorem 7 of irreducible SU(2)^2 × U(1)-invariant SU(2) G2-instantons with bounded curvature that extend smoothly over P1, where near t = 0 their local data satisfy f^+(t) = f1^+ t + O(t^3) and g^+(t) = g1^+ t + O(t^3). Can the resulting noncompact end of M_P1^{BGGG} be compactified by analyzing sequences for which f1^+ tends to +infinity and/or g1^+ tends to +infinity? More precisely, after suitable rescaling transverse to the associative S^3, do such sequences exhibit a Bryant–Salamon-type analogue of Theorem 6—namely bubbling of anti-self-dual instantons together with convergence away from S^3 to a limiting G2-instanton—with possible bubbles related to the ASD instantons on Taub–NUT constructed by Etesi–Hausel? ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Section 4.4(f), whose wording is already very close to your version: compactify the noncompact BGGG moduli-space end by studying the Theorem 7 family as f1^+ and/or g1^+ go to infinity, expecting Bryant–Salamon-type bubbling possibly related to Taub–NUT ASD instantons. The nearby context needed to make this stand-alone comes from Lemma 3 and Proposition 12, which define the local parameters f1^+, g1^+ and the 2-parameter local family extending over P1, and from Theorem 6, which is the explicit Bryant–Salamon bubbling model being invoked. The only substantial correction is that Section 4.4(d) leaves part of M_P1^{BGGG} unresolved, so the sharpest formulation is about the known noncompact end from Theorem 7, or about the full moduli space conditional on first describing that remaining region. No ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, or nilpotency hypotheses are relevant here; this is a differential-geometric moduli and compactness question. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
